label: copy phase of length-3 sequences (strongest at the final output)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L), never on original tokens or the <DEL> step, and never on the first occurrence of a token. Its core is copy steps of the shortest sequences (L=3): 27% of L=3 steps are active, and they carry about 63% of activation mass. The largest activations (near max) fall at t=5, the final output of an L=3 sequence (97% precision there, 48% of mass), and the t=4 step is weaker. In longer sequences it fires weakly and sparsely, mostly on the last one or two copy steps (to_go <= 1), and more often when the input token is g, q, n or l. Adding that tail to the predicate raises mass recall to about 0.85 but drops precision to about 0.28, so it is left out. It does not fire in the original or delimiter phases. Dev results for (L==3)&(phase==2): P=0.82, R=0.33, mass recall 0.63.
